common_name: Miss Manila Bougainvillea (Compact Coral-Pink Everblooming Bougainvillea)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. Miss Manila is a Philippine-bred cultivar popular as a compact hedge, mounding shrub, or container plant.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. Miss Manila produces an abundance of soft coral-pink bracts on a naturally mounding, moderately compact plant that can be grown as a free-standing shrub, low hedge, or trained onto a small trellis, and it is exceptionally heavy-blooming even without much pruning. Its manageable size and dense bract coverage have made it a widely planted landscape bougainvillea across the Gulf South and Florida, where it thrives in heat and tolerates poor, sandy soil. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production, and protect from hard freezes since it is one of the more tender bougainvillea cultivars.

common_name: La Jolla Bougainvillea (Compact Deep Magenta-Red Bougainvillea)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. La Jolla is a compact, dense-branching cultivar popular for hedges and containers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. La Jolla produces heavy clusters of deep magenta-red bracts on a compact, dense, well-branched plant that stays manageable as a low hedge, mounding shrub, or container specimen without the sprawling reach of vining bougainvillea cultivars. Its tight branching and heavy bloom have made it a popular choice for foundation plantings and mass landscaping in warm coastal climates. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production, and protect from hard freezes.

common_name: Raspberry Ice Bougainvillea (Variegated Cream-Edged Foliage Pink Bougainvillea)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. Raspberry Ice offers variegated foliage interest even when not in bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. Raspberry Ice bears leaves edged in a creamy white variegation year-round, providing ornamental interest even between bloom flushes, and produces raspberry-pink bracts that contrast attractively against the pale-margined foliage. Its variegated leaves make it useful as a foliage accent trained on a trellis or fence in addition to its floral display. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production, and protect from hard freezes since variegated cultivars can be somewhat less vigorous than solid-green types.

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. Silhouette offers striking variegated foliage interest even when not in bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. Silhouette bears leaves boldly edged in crisp white variegation surrounding a green center, a striking foliage pattern that stands out even before the plant produces its clusters of red to purple-red bracts. The strong foliage contrast makes it a useful accent trained on a trellis, arbor, or fence where its variegated leaves provide interest between bloom cycles. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production, and protect from hard freezes since variegated cultivars can be somewhat less vigorous than solid-green types.

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun; bougainvilleas bloom most prolifically under slight water and fertilizer stress. Mrs. Butt is a long-established crimson-red cultivar and parent behind several later bougainvillea sports.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, lean soil in full sun. Mrs. Butt is a long-established, deep crimson-red bougainvillea cultivar with a vigorous, thorny, sprawling growth habit typical of older bougainvillea varieties bred for covering a large arbor, wall, or fence rather than staying compact. Its historic significance comes from being an early, widely distributed red cultivar that served as parent stock for several later bougainvillea sports and selections. As with other bougainvillea, avoid overwatering and excess nitrogen fertilizer, both of which push leafy growth at the expense of bract production, and give it plenty of room and a sturdy structure to climb given its vigorous mature size.
